messages:
evan: Heads up — after last night's maintenance cold-boot on rack-7b we're seeing a spike in Xid 31 on nodes g7b-03..g7b-06. Fail rate ~1.8% for tenant batch-encoder jobs. Anyone else notice this?

claire: saw the alerts at 02:30 UTC, digging now. dmesg on g7b-05 shows a lot of `NVRM: Xid 31` interleaved with NIC link flaps.

sanjay: ipmitool sensors look ok for temps, fans are high (95%) on those hosts. PSU B shows current draw spikes coincident with some Xid entries.

opsbot: Note: automated maintenance action: cold-boot executed on rack-7b at 02:12 UTC (runbook: kernel+driver reboot).

evan: quick error sample from g7b-05 (dmesg tail):
```
[Feb08 02:28:14] NVRM: Xid (31): M0:00000002 0x00000000 0x00000000
[Feb08 02:28:14] NVRM: Xid (31) on ch 0000:81:00.0
[Feb08 02:28:14] e1000e 0000:3b:00.0 NIC Link is Down
[Feb08 02:28:15] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x1e1)
```

liam: Which NVIDIA driver/kernel versions are those nodes on? Could be a driver regression affecting decode paths under long-sequence decoder workloads.

evan: driver 535.86.05, kernel 6.5.2 (same as the maintenance roll last night). Other racks with different workload mix are fine.

claire: early hypothesis: workload-sensitive failure — long-lived KV cache + large batch sizes trigger sustained memory access pattern that surfaces an Xid 31 (MRB -> memory read barrier). Sanity check: can we repro by running the tenant encoder job locally on a suspect node with `batch=64`?

sanjay: ran a quick local run with batch=64 -> Xid reproduced within ~90s. Reduced to batch=16 -> no Xid in 10m. Suggests pressure-related.

evan: mitigation plan I pushed: draining g7b-03..g7b-06 from batch-encoder routing, set routing policy to prefer other racks for encoder workload, and set temporary per-tenant max_batch=32. Also opened INF-7234.

hw-ops: we'll schedule a slot to swap g7b-05 GPU tomorrow if errors persist after reroute. Please capture `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF,RET` and syslogs for the window before swap.

claire: also going to run driver rollback test on a single node (rollback to 532.x) in canary to see if issue is driver-introduced. Will report back in this thread.

evan: thanks — keeping the thread here. If anyone sees `Xid 13` or `48` patterns in the same hosts, ping — could be multiple failure modes but current correlation looks batch-size / sustained-workload related after cold-boot. :thumbsup:

opsbot: Reaction: :rotating_light: alert suppressed for drained nodes.
